result.topic_en: From Ramanujan's work on highly composite numbers: an asymptotic formula for log Σ_{-s}(N), the maximal value of the sum of the (−s)-th powers of divisors, followed by the case 0 < s < 1/2.
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94 $^{18\,(45)}$ (45) (89)
By arguments similar to those of §42 we can show that
$S_s(x_1) = S_s\{\log N + O\sqrt{x_1}(\log x_1)^2\} = S_s(\log N) + O\{x_1^{-s}(\log x_1)^4\}$.
Hence
(377) $\log \Sigma_{-s}(N) = \log|\zeta(s)| + Li(\log N)^{1-s} - \frac{1}{2}Li(\log N)^{1-2s} + \frac{1}{3}Li(\log N)^{1-3s}$
$- \cdots\cdots - \frac{(-1)^n}{n}Li(\log N)^{1-ns} - \frac{1}{2}Li(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}$
$+ \frac{(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s} + S_s(\log N)}{\log\log N} + Li(x_2^{1-2s}) - \frac{x_2(\log N)^{-s}}{\log\log N}$
$+ O\left\{\frac{(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log\log N)^2}\right\}$,
where $n = [1+\frac{1}{2s}]$ and
(378) $x_2 = 2^{1/(2s)}\sqrt{x_1} + O\left(\frac{\sqrt{x_1}}{\log x_1}\right) = 2^{1/(2s)}\sqrt{(\log N)} + O\left\{\frac{\sqrt{(\log N)}}{\log\log N}\right\}$
in virtue of (365).
71. Let us consider the order of $\Sigma_{-s}(N)$ in the following 3 cases.
Case I $0 < s < \frac{1}{2}$.
Here we have
$Li(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s} = \frac{(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\frac{1}{2}-s)\log\log N} + O\left\{\frac{(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log\log N)^2}\right\}$.
$Li(x_2^{1-2s}) = \frac{x_2^{1-2s}}{(1-2s)\log x_2} + O\left\{\frac{x_2^{1-2s}}{(\log x_2)^2}\right\}$
$= \frac{2^{1/(2s)}(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(1-2s)\log\log N} + O\left\{\frac{(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log\log N)^2}\right\}$.
$\frac{x_2(\log N)^{-s}}{\log\log N} = \frac{2^{1/(2s)}(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{\log\log N} + O\left\{\frac{(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log\log N)^2}\right\}$
It follows from these and (377) that
(379) $\log \Sigma_{-s}(N) = Li(\log N)^{1-s} - \frac{1}{2}Li(\log N)^{1-2s} + \frac{1}{3}Li(\log N)^{1-3s}$
$- \cdots\cdots\cdots - \frac{(-1)^n}{n}Li(\log N)^{1-ns}$
$- \frac{2s(2^{1/(2s)}-1)(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(1-2s)\log\log N} + \frac{S_s(\log N)}{\log\log N} + O\left\{\frac{(\log N)^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log\log N)^2}\right\}$
where $n = [1+\frac{1}{2s}]$. Remembering (358) and (378) and making
$s \to \frac{1}{2}$ in (377) we have
